title: Investor pitch
summary: Pitch your seed round to a skeptical partner and a numbers focused associate.
goal: Get a partner meeting next week to discuss terms for our seed round.
scenario: You're raising a 1.5 million dollar seed round for a scheduling tool for clinics. You have 40 paying clinics.

attendees.name: Rhea
likely_objections: Clinic software is a crowded market
Forty clinics is early; is this a feature or a company?
Why can't an incumbent add this in a quarter?
attendees.knows: Read the one page summary, not the deck. Has seen two clinic scheduling pitches this year. Will only take it to the partner meeting if the market and the team both hold up.

attendees.name: Tom
likely_objections: How long until a clinic pays back what it cost to win?
How much of the round goes to sales versus product?
attendees.knows: Built a model from the data room. Noticed churn looks low but the cohort is young.

hidden_concerns: Market size and how it was calculated
success: Rhea agrees to a partner meeting or a terms discussion with a date.
tips: Open with the ask, the traction and why now, in under a minute.
Answer every number question with the number first, then the context.
End by asking for a specific next step and a date.

key_facts.label: Growth
key_facts.value: 15 percent month over month for 6 months

ask: A partner meeting next week to discuss terms.
